topic: History of Bharat Ratna and Padma Awards
description: This topic covers the history, categories, significant recipients, and constitutional provisions related to India's highest civilian honours. It is an essential component of Static GK for competitive exams.

sections.title: Background of Civilian Honours
sections.description: The institution, classification, and historical timeline of the highest civilian awards established by the Government of India in 1954.

key_concepts.explanation: The highest civilian award of India, awarded in recognition of exceptional service or performance of the highest order in any field of human endeavour.
The next highest civilian awards given after the Bharat Ratna, categorized hierarchically into three tiers: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri.

historical_events.significance: The Bharat Ratna and Padma Awards were instituted by the then President of India, Dr. Rajendra Prasad.
The awards were briefly suspended during the Morarji Desai government and later due to pending Public Interest Litigations (PILs) in the Supreme Court.

sections.title: Bharat Ratna: Important Facts
sections.description: Crucial details regarding the medallion's design and historical 'firsts' among its recipients.

key_concepts.explanation: The award is shaped like a Peepal leaf, cast in bronze. Its obverse features a sunburst design with the words 'Bharat Ratna' inscribed in Devanagari script.

important_facts.fact: The first recipients in 1954 were C. Rajagopalachari, Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, and C. V. Raman.
Former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri became the first individual to be honoured with the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 1966.
Indira Gandhi was the first woman to receive the Bharat Ratna (1971).
Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (Frontier Gandhi) became the first non-Indian (foreigner) to receive the award in 1987.
Sachin Tendulkar is the first sportsperson and the youngest individual (at age 40) to receive the Bharat Ratna.

sections.title: Hierarchy and Rules of Padma Awards
sections.description: Details on the three categories of Padma Awards and the general guidelines for conferring them.

key_concepts.explanation: The second-highest civilian award in India, given for 'exceptional and distinguished service'.
The third-highest civilian award, given for 'distinguished service of a high order'.
The fourth-highest civilian award, given for 'distinguished service' in any field.

important_facts.fact: The Padma Awards are announced annually on the eve of Republic Day (26th January).
The total number of Padma Awards given in a year (excluding posthumous awards and to NRI/foreigners/OCIs) should not exceed 120.

sections.title: Constitutional Provisions and Judicial Decisions
sections.description: The legal validity of these civilian awards and their relationship with the Fundamental Rights of the Indian Constitution.

polity_articles.provision: Abolition of Titles: No title, not being a military or academic distinction, shall be conferred by the State.
polity_articles.details: National awards like Bharat Ratna and Padma Awards are not considered 'titles' under this article and cannot be used as prefixes or suffixes to the recipient's name.

historical_events.event: Balaji Raghavan vs Union of India Case
historical_events.significance: The Supreme Court of India upheld the constitutional validity of the national awards, ruling that they do not amount to 'titles' within the meaning of Article 18(1).

sections.title: Distinguished Recipients and Related Facts
sections.description: A quick look at frequently asked questions regarding prominent personalities who have received these honours.

important_facts.fact: In 1992, Subhas Chandra Bose was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously, but it was later cancelled by a Supreme Court order due to the controversy surrounding his death, making it the only case of a withdrawn Bharat Ratna.
